title: Music Playlist
story: You just discovered an underground band and want to track their best songs. Each song has a title, artist, and duration. Your music app needs to format song info nicely so you can build a playlist and share it with friends.
why: A struct with a formatting method is the foundation of every data display system.
analogy: A Song struct is like a CD case (or a streaming card). The title is printed on the front, the artist is below it, and the duration is stamped on the spine. The format method reads the card aloud.
try_it: Add your top 3 favorite songs with real titles and artists. Add a `Song.genre(self) -> Str` field to the struct (use a genre enum: Rock, Pop, Electronic, Jazz). Add a method that returns whether the song is longer than 4 minutes.
tips: Use `duration_sec / 60` for minutes and `duration_sec % 60` for remaining seconds
Escape double quotes inside strings with `\"` to display the title in quotes
Longer song durations make for more interesting total runtime calculations
common_mistakes: Forgetting the `% 60` on seconds — without modulo, seconds show numbers like 75 instead of 15
Putting the artist name inside the title field — keep fields separate for clean data
